query: How does incident resolution efficiency vary across category, priority, and assignment group?

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Resolution hours is essentially the operationalization of resolution efficiency itself (the inverse of speed), not an external associational variable. It restates the focus rather than opening a relationship to segment against, and its continuous, near-unique values offer no interpretable categories for grouping.

per_column.name: efficiency_category
per_column.rationale: This is a binned version of the focus variable (Slow/Normal), i.e. a direct restatement of resolution efficiency. While categorical, it is the focus itself, not an independent explanatory dimension to compare it against.

per_column.name: priority_level
per_column.rationale: Priority is already present in the original table (priority) and named as a query dimension; this merely duplicates it. It has well-separated interpretable categories, but it adds no new external variable beyond what already exists.

per_column.name: efficiency_score
per_column.rationale: An opaque numeric score that is itself the focus (efficiency), not an external segmentation variable. Its fine-grained, near-unique values provide no interpretable categories for human exploration and restate the target.

judge.rationale: None of the added columns introduce an external, associational variable that can be grouped and compared against resolution efficiency. resolution_hours, efficiency_category, and efficiency_score are all restatements/operationalizations of the focus itself, and priority_level merely duplicates an existing original column. The set fails the exploratory-analysis claim because it does not open up any new interpretable relationship for a human explorer; it circles around the focus rather than providing independent dimensions to segment on.
